reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 110 --verse 10.44.6 (Sāyaṇa sa.wikisource rev 328215 and Sarup's Nirukta 5.25). The reading half stands: Sāyaṇa's words carry 'without Indra's grace' (tvatprasādarahitā janāḥ), 'evildoers' (pāpakarmāṇo janāḥ) and 'sunk low by debt' (ṛṇenaiva nyaviśanta nīcair aviśanta, adhogatiṃ prāptāḥ); Sarup's Yāska carries 'remained here, in this very place, or in debt, or in this world'; Sāyaṇa himself cites nir. 5.25, so the locator holds; the difference (Sāyaṇa narrows to debt and adds grace and evildoing, Yāska leaves this world as an option) is named, not resolved. verse.js ok (10.44.6, [880,6]); entry-check ok, 55 words. The plain half lands under rule 2 and the plan trap: 'the singer sets the first callers of the gods against those who failed to board and sank' is a line-by-line paraphrase of the key verse printed just above it, not context, and 'callers' is the commentators' agentive gloss (Sāyaṇa: devānām āhvātāraḥ, kartari kṛt; Yāska: 'who invoked the gods') where Griffith's text says 'invocation', so the plain sense restates the commentator's reading instead of the day's text in its own terms.
better: Keep the reading half; replace the plain clause with context from the hymn itself, e.g. 'Between the call for Indra to sit on the holy grass and the wish that the evil-hearted stay far away, the singer contrasts two fates at the sacrifice;' then re-run entry-check (four-word runs, 60-word cap).
